components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Used for main actions like generating plans or saving.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #2563eb, #4e8ef7); color: #fff; padding: 6px 16px; border: 1px solid #4e8ef7; border-radius: 6px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: all 180ms ease; box-shadow: 0 0 24px rgba(78, 142, 247, 0.2), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.04); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4e8ef7, #6da3ff); transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 0 32px rgba(78, 142, 247, 0.35), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.04); }

narrative.overview: The design system exudes technical precision, reliability, and expert confidence. It's built for functionality, centering the 3D visualizer while maintaining an interface that feels robust and structural. It explicitly avoids feeling like an overwhelming CAD tool or a cartoonish toy.
keyCharacteristics: Layered surfaces using glassmorphism for depth

rules.name: The Expert Restraint Rule
rules.body: Color is functional, never purely decorative. Use semantic colors (amber, green, red) strictly for their meaning, not for generic branding.

rules.name: The Glass Canvas Rule
rules.body: UI panels floating over the 3D viewport must use glassmorphism (translucency + background blur) to maintain the user's spatial awareness of the structure underneath.

dos: Do rely on structural borders and precise spacing to group information.
Do keep error messages educational and focused on safety.
donts: Don't use overly playful or cartoonish interfaces.
Don't create overwhelming, dense CAD-like panels that crowd the screen.
Don't obscure the 3D visualizer completely; it is the hero.
